A Digital Home for India's Living Heritage

Bharat Vividha

Our Culture. Our Pride. Our Future.

One map, one trusted source, one journey — bringing together India's monuments and temples alongside its festivals, folk arts, crafts, languages and cuisines, so that what is seen and what is felt can finally be discovered together.

See what it brings together Read the approach

Most of India's heritage is never found

Each generation grows up knowing a handful of famous monuments, while thousands of lesser-known traditions, local histories, dialects and dishes stay undocumented — scattered across sources that rarely speak to one another.

For a traveller, the search for heritage and the planning of a trip live in separate places entirely, so a nearby but unfamiliar site is easy to miss, hard to understand, and harder still to visit responsibly.

Bharat Vividha closes that gap: a single digital space combining verified information from government and academic sources with the lived knowledge of local communities.

heritage sites in the first release, built to expand nationwide over time.

What Bharat Vividha brings into one place

Visible heritage — monuments, temples, archaeological and natural sites — and living heritage — festivals, folk arts, music, rituals, crafts, language and food — shown together, the way they're actually experienced.

About this dataset — this is a curated starting set of nationally and regionally significant sites, not an exhaustive record of every district's heritage. If a district shows no results, it likely means it isn't in this dataset yet rather than that it has no heritage worth noting.

The first release, and how it's built

Designed for the Smart India Hackathon 2026, using proven, easily extensible technology so it can grow from a first release into a nationwide platform.

01

Map-based heritage search

A geospatial database lets users search their own surroundings for traditional and lesser-known sites.

02

Detailed, verified listings

Written, photo, audio and video information for each site, checked against reliable sources.

03

Trip planning

General itinerary building around chosen heritage sites and interests.

04

Cultural chatbot & image recognition

An AI assistant for questions, and photo-based identification of monuments and artefacts.

05

Administrative tools

Systems for managing and verifying contributed information.

Built for mobile and web alike

Location detection, offline access and map-based search work across both, backed by a geospatial database purpose-built for storing and querying place-based heritage data.

Risks are treated as design problems, not afterthoughts: misinformation, AI bias, cultural insensitivity and over-tourism are all addressed through verification and human oversight, from day one.

Built on responsible use

Bharat Vividha is not just a travel tool. It joins heritage, living culture, local knowledge, trip planning, AI and mapping into a single responsible practice.

Sustainable tourism

Promoting lesser-known destinations to ease pressure on the same handful of famous sites.

Local participation

Communities contribute knowledge and benefit directly from the attention it brings.

Cultural sensitivity

Traditions are represented in their own context, not flattened for convenience.

Privacy & verification

User-contributed information is checked, and personal privacy is protected throughout.

Who it's built for

From first-time travellers to the researchers and policymakers working to preserve what they study.

Travellers

Discover nearby heritage worth the detour, and plan around it.

Students & researchers

A verified reference for history, culture and local tradition.

Local communities

New visibility and economic opportunity for artisans and villages.

Policymakers

A clearer picture of heritage assets worth protecting and promoting.

Ask the Cultural Guide

A working preview of the AI cultural assistant. Ask about any Indian monument, festival, tradition, or place — it answers from general knowledge, not from the site's own dataset.

Namaste! Ask me about a monument, festival, region, or tradition — for example, "What is Bishnupur famous for?" or "When is Durga Puja celebrated?"

Powered by a serverless function — the API key stays on the server, never in this page.
